questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: The branch of literature concerned with performance on a stage, involving dialogue and action, is called
questions.explanation: Drama is the literary genre written primarily to be performed by actors before an audience.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A literary work written in narrative form, using ordinary spoken or written language rather than verse, is called
questions.explanation: Prose is language in its ordinary, unmetred form, as used in novels and short stories, distinguished from the structured lines of poetry.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A composition that uses condensed, rhythmic, and often figurative language, typically arranged in lines and stanzas, is called
questions.explanation: Poetry is characterised by its use of rhythm, imagery, and compressed, often figurative, language, structured into lines and stanzas.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: The plot structure of a typical play, in order, moves through exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, and
questions.explanation: The denouement, or resolution, is the final stage of a plot where the conflicts are resolved and loose ends are tied up.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: The point of highest tension or the turning point in a plot is called the
questions.explanation: The climax is the decisive moment of greatest intensity in a narrative, after which the action begins to fall toward resolution.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A brief, indirect reference to a person, event, or work outside the text is called
questions.explanation: An allusion is a passing reference to another work, person, or event that the writer expects the reader to recognise and connect with.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A statement that appears self-contradictory but reveals an underlying truth is called a
questions.explanation: A paradox seems logically contradictory on the surface, yet expresses a deeper or unexpected truth, e.g., 'less is more.'

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A word or phrase that has become overused to the point of losing its original impact is called a
questions.explanation: A cliché is an expression so frequently used that it has lost its freshness and persuasive force, such as 'as light as a feather.'

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A recurring element, such as an image, idea, or situation, that helps develop a text's central theme is called a
questions.explanation: A motif is a recurring symbol, idea, or image that reinforces the central theme(s) of a literary work.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: The repetition of a line or group of lines at intervals in a poem, especially at the end of each stanza, is called a
questions.explanation: A refrain is a line or set of lines repeated at regular intervals throughout a poem or song, often for emphasis or musicality.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A pause or break within a line of poetry, often marked by punctuation, is called a
questions.explanation: A caesura is a natural pause within a line of verse, frequently created by punctuation such as a comma or full stop.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: When a sentence or clause continues beyond the end of a line of poetry without a pause, this is called
questions.explanation: Enjambment occurs when a thought or grammatical unit runs on from one line of poetry into the next without a terminal pause.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: The repetition of similar vowel sounds in nearby words is known as
questions.explanation: Assonance is the repetition of vowel sounds within nearby words, as in 'the rain in Spain', creating internal musicality.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: The repetition of similar consonant sounds, especially at the end of words, is known as
questions.explanation: Consonance repeats consonant sounds, typically at the end or middle of words, distinct from alliteration, which repeats initial sounds.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A two-line unit of verse, usually rhyming and containing a complete thought, is called a
questions.explanation: A couplet consists of two successive rhymed lines, often forming a self-contained unit of meaning.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A fourteen-line poem, often written in iambic pentameter and associated with themes of love, is called a
questions.explanation: The sonnet is a fixed fourteen-line poetic form, popularised in English by Shakespeare, traditionally exploring love and related themes.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A poem of mourning written to lament the death of a person is called an
questions.explanation: An elegy is a poem of serious reflection, typically a lament for someone who has died.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A long narrative poem celebrating the deeds of a legendary or historical hero is called an
questions.explanation: An epic is a lengthy narrative poem recounting the heroic deeds and adventures of a legendary or historical figure, such as Homer's Iliad.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A short, simple narrative poem, often set to music and dealing with folk stories, is called a
questions.explanation: A ballad is a narrative poem, traditionally sung, that tells a story in simple stanzas, often drawn from folklore or popular tradition.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A formal, elaborate lyric poem written in praise of, or addressed to, a particular subject is called an
questions.explanation: An ode is a dignified, often ceremonious lyric poem that celebrates or reflects deeply on its subject.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: The use of words whose sound imitates the sound they describe, such as 'buzz' or 'crash', is called
questions.explanation: Onomatopoeia refers to words that phonetically resemble the sound they represent, adding sensory immediacy to writing.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A short speech in which a character, alone on stage, expresses inner thoughts directly to the audience is a
questions.explanation: A soliloquy is delivered by a character alone on stage, revealing private thoughts and motivations to the audience.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A long, uninterrupted speech given by one character to other characters (or the audience) within a scene is a
questions.explanation: A monologue is an extended speech by a single character, which, unlike a soliloquy, may be addressed to other characters present.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A remark made by a character, intended to be heard by the audience but not by other characters on stage, is an
questions.explanation: An aside is a brief comment directed to the audience that other characters on stage are conventionally understood not to hear.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: The narrator who uses 'I' and participates directly in the events of the story is called a
questions.explanation: A first-person narrator tells the story from their own point of view using 'I', often as a character within the events narrated.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A narrator who knows the thoughts and feelings of all characters in a story is described as
questions.explanation: A third-person omniscient narrator has unrestricted access to the thoughts, feelings, and motives of every character in the narrative.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A character whose personal moral flaw or error in judgement leads to their eventual downfall in a tragedy displays
questions.explanation: Hamartia is the tragic flaw or mistaken judgement in a protagonist that sets their downfall in motion.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: The sudden reversal of fortune experienced by the protagonist in a tragedy is known, in Aristotelian terms, as
questions.explanation: Peripeteia refers to the abrupt reversal of circumstances or fortune for the protagonist, a key turning point in classical tragedy.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: The moment in a tragedy when a character discovers a crucial truth previously hidden from them is called
questions.explanation: Anagnorisis is the moment of critical discovery or recognition, often when a character learns their true identity or situation.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Two contrasting ideas, words, or images placed close together for emphasis form a literary device called
questions.explanation: Juxtaposition places two elements side by side to highlight their differences or create a particular effect through contrast.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A figure of speech combining two normally contradictory terms, such as 'deafening silence', is called an
questions.explanation: An oxymoron pairs two seemingly contradictory words together for rhetorical or dramatic effect.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A play in which the central character suffers a serious downfall, often ending in death, best describes the genre of
questions.explanation: Tragedy centres on a protagonist's serious downfall, typically arising from a flaw or a combination of adverse circumstances.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A humorous work that ends happily, often involving misunderstandings that are eventually resolved, is a
questions.explanation: Comedy uses humour and light-hearted conflict, generally resolving in a happy or favourable outcome for the main characters.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A literary work that uses humour, irony, or exaggeration to criticise human vice or folly is a
questions.explanation: Satire employs wit, irony, or ridicule to expose and criticise human weaknesses, societal vices, or institutions.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A character who serves as a contrast to another character, highlighting particular qualities by comparison, is called a
questions.explanation: A foil is a character whose traits contrast with those of another character, thereby emphasising the qualities of that other character.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: The play 'Death and the King's Horseman' was written by
questions.explanation: Death and the King's Horseman is a tragedy by the Nigerian Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka, based on real events in colonial Oyo.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: 'Death and the King's Horseman' is set in the Yoruba town of
questions.explanation: The play is set in the ancient Yoruba town of Oyo during the colonial period, drawing on a historical incident that occurred there.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: In 'Death and the King's Horseman', Elesin Oba is expected to die by ritual suicide in order to
options: avenge a personal insult from the colonial officer
accompany his dead king into the afterlife as tradition demands
escape punishment for a crime he committed
fulfil a debt owed to the market women
questions.explanation: Yoruba custom requires the King's Horseman, Elesin, to take his own life so that his spirit can accompany the deceased king, maintaining cosmic order.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: In 'Death and the King's Horseman', the British colonial officer who intervenes to stop the ritual suicide is
questions.explanation: Simon Pilkings, the District Officer, disrupts the ritual by arresting Elesin, misunderstanding and interfering with Yoruba custom.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: In 'Death and the King's Horseman', Olunde is significant because he
options: is Elesin's son, who returns from studying medicine in England to complete the ritual his father failed to fulfil
refuses to accept any Yoruba tradition
questions.explanation: Olunde, educated in England, ultimately takes his own life in his father's place to preserve the honour Elesin failed to uphold.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Wole Soyinka's play 'The Lion and the Jewel' centres on a rivalry between Baroka and Lakunle over
questions.explanation: The Lion and the Jewel is a comedy in which the old chief Baroka and the young schoolteacher Lakunle both seek to win Sidi, the beautiful village belle.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: In 'The Lion and the Jewel', Baroka is best described as
options: the shrewd, traditionalist village chief nicknamed 'the Lion'
questions.explanation: Baroka, the Bale (chief) of Ilujinle, is a cunning and traditionalist elder who ultimately outwits his younger rival for Sidi's affection.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Ola Rotimi's play 'The Gods Are Not to Blame' is a reworking of which classical Greek tragedy?
questions.explanation: The Gods Are Not to Blame transposes the story of Sophocles' Oedipus Rex into a Yoruba setting, centring on King Odewale.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: In 'The Gods Are Not to Blame', King Odewale unknowingly fulfils a prophecy by
options: betraying his kingdom to a rival tribe
murdering his own son in battle
killing his real father and marrying his real mother
starting a war with a neighbouring village
questions.explanation: Like Oedipus, Odewale unwittingly kills his biological father and marries his mother, fulfilling the very prophecy he sought to avoid.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Efua Sutherland, celebrated for the play 'The Marriage of Anansewa', was a playwright from
questions.explanation: Efua Sutherland was a prominent Ghanaian dramatist and a key figure in the development of modern African theatre.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: In Efua Sutherland's 'The Marriage of Anansewa', the character Ananse tries to profit by
options: selling his farmland to the highest bidder
arranging his daughter's marriage to multiple wealthy suitors simultaneously for gifts
questions.explanation: Ananse, a trickster figure drawn from Akan folklore, schemes to betroth his daughter Anansewa to several rich suitors at once to extract gifts from each.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: James Ene Henshaw's play 'This is Our Chance' primarily explores the theme of
options: the aftermath of a civil war
conflict between traditional customs and modern/Western values
corruption within a colonial police force
the horrors of the transatlantic slave trade
questions.explanation: This is Our Chance dramatises the tension between an older generation's traditional customs and a younger generation's embrace of modern ideas.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: The Nigerian playwright known for 'Song of a Goat' and 'The Raft', reflecting on fate and community life in the Niger Delta, is
questions.explanation: J.P. Clark, a Niger Delta poet and dramatist, explores themes of destiny and communal life in plays such as Song of a Goat and The Raft.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Zulu Sofola, one of Nigeria's earliest published female playwrights, is known for works such as
questions.explanation: Zulu Sofola's Wedlock of the Gods examines the tragic consequences of forbidden love within the constraints of traditional custom.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Wole Soyinka's satirical play 'The Trials of Brother Jero' centres on a character who is a
questions.explanation: Brother Jero is a comic, manipulative 'prophet' who exploits his gullible followers on the beach for his own personal gain.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: William Shakespeare's tragedy 'Hamlet' centres on a Danish prince who seeks revenge for the murder of his
questions.explanation: Hamlet is driven by the ghost of his murdered father's revelation and his subsequent quest to avenge the killing, committed by his uncle Claudius.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: In Shakespeare's 'Hamlet', Claudius murders King Hamlet, his brother, chiefly in order to
options: avenge an old insult from the king
seize the throne of Denmark and marry Queen Gertrude
fulfil a prophecy given by the ghost
protect Denmark from a foreign invasion
questions.explanation: Claudius poisons his brother, King Hamlet, to claim both the Danish throne and Gertrude, the widowed queen.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Shakespeare's tragedy 'Macbeth' depicts the downfall of a Scottish general driven primarily by
options: unrequited love for a rival's daughter
ambition, spurred on by prophecy and his wife's persuasion
questions.explanation: Macbeth's tragic downfall stems from unchecked ambition, ignited by the witches' prophecy and intensified by Lady Macbeth's urging.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: In 'Macbeth', the three witches first hail Macbeth with prophecies concerning his future as
options: Earl of Gloucester and future Pope
Duke of Cornwall and Prince of Wales
Thane of Cawdor and future King of Scotland
questions.explanation: The witches greet Macbeth as Thane of Glamis, Thane of Cawdor, and 'king hereafter', setting his ambitions in motion.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Shakespeare's tragedy 'Othello' centres on a Moorish general whose downfall is engineered by his manipulative ensign,
questions.explanation: Iago manipulates Othello into a jealous rage over his wife Desdemona through deceit, ultimately causing Othello's tragic downfall.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: In Shakespeare's 'Othello', Othello is ultimately driven to kill his wife, Desdemona, because he wrongly believes she has been
options: conspiring with her father against him
questions.explanation: Deceived by Iago's false evidence, Othello wrongly believes Desdemona has committed adultery with Cassio, leading him to murder her.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Shakespeare's play 'Romeo and Juliet' tells the tragic story of two young lovers from feuding families in the city of
questions.explanation: Romeo and Juliet is set in Verona, Italy, where the feuding Montague and Capulet families drive the young lovers to their tragic end.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: In Shakespeare's 'Julius Caesar', Caesar is assassinated by a group of conspirators led by Cassius and, notably, his trusted friend
questions.explanation: Marcus Brutus, Caesar's close friend, joins the conspiracy out of a belief that Caesar's growing power threatens the Roman republic.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Henrik Ibsen's play 'A Doll's House' is best known for its portrayal of
options: a soldier's return from a foreign war
a woman's awakening to the constraints of her marriage and society
questions.explanation: A Doll's House follows Nora Helmer as she comes to recognise the oppressive, patronising nature of her marriage, ultimately leaving her husband and children.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: In Ibsen's 'A Doll's House', Nora Helmer famously ends the play by
options: being sent away by her husband to an asylum
reconciling fully and happily with her husband Torvald
dying of an illness she had concealed
walking out of her marriage and family home to seek her own identity
questions.explanation: Nora's departure, slamming the door behind her, is one of the most famous and controversial endings in modern drama.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Arthur Miller's play 'Death of a Salesman' explores the tragic disillusionment of an ageing salesman named
questions.explanation: Death of a Salesman centres on Willy Loman, whose pursuit of the American Dream ends in personal and professional collapse.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Arthur Miller's play 'The Crucible' uses the Salem witch trials to allegorically comment on
options: the McCarthyist anti-communist hysteria of 1950s America
the horrors of the First World War
questions.explanation: The Crucible dramatises the 1692 Salem witch trials as an allegory for the paranoia and false accusations of the McCarthy era.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: George Bernard Shaw's play 'Pygmalion', which inspired the musical 'My Fair Lady', follows a phonetics professor who transforms a
options: servant boy into a member of royalty
young soldier into a decorated general
Cockney flower girl into a woman who can pass as a duchess
poor farmer into a wealthy landowner
questions.explanation: In Pygmalion, Professor Henry Higgins trains flower-seller Eliza Doolittle to speak and behave so as to pass for a high-society lady.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Oscar Wilde's comedy 'The Importance of Being Earnest' is celebrated chiefly for its
options: witty dialogue and satire of Victorian social conventions
questions.explanation: The Importance of Being Earnest is a comedy of manners known for its epigrammatic wit and satirical treatment of Victorian upper-class hypocrisy.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Sophocles' Greek tragedy 'Antigone' centres on a woman who defies the king's decree in order to
options: give her brother a proper burial
questions.explanation: Antigone defies King Creon's edict forbidding the burial of her brother Polynices, choosing familial and religious duty over the law of the state.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Chinua Achebe's novel 'Things Fall Apart' centres on a proud Igbo wrestler and farmer named
questions.explanation: Things Fall Apart follows Okonkwo, a respected and fiercely proud man in the village of Umuofia, whose life is disrupted by the arrival of colonialism.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: In 'Things Fall Apart', Okonkwo's downfall is driven largely by his fear of resembling his father, who was seen as
options: a coward who fled from war
questions.explanation: Okonkwo's relentless drive for status stems from his determination not to be like his gentle, improvident father, Unoka, whom the village considered a failure.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: 'Things Fall Apart' is set in the fictional Igbo village of
questions.explanation: The novel is set primarily in Umuofia, a fictional cluster of Igbo villages representing pre-colonial and colonial-era Igbo society.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: At the end of 'Things Fall Apart', Okonkwo ultimately
options: is exiled permanently to his mother's village
becomes the new leader of his clan
hangs himself after killing a colonial court messenger
questions.explanation: Unable to accept his clan's growing passivity toward colonial rule, Okonkwo kills a court messenger and, in despair, takes his own life.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Chinua Achebe's novel 'No Longer at Ease' follows Obi Okonkwo, grandson of the protagonist of 'Things Fall Apart', as he struggles with
options: a civil war between rival ethnic groups
corruption and the pressures of urban life in colonial-era Lagos
questions.explanation: No Longer at Ease follows Obi Okonkwo's moral compromise amid financial pressure and bureaucratic corruption in colonial Lagos.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Chinua Achebe's novel about the Nigerian Civil War's shattered idealism, focusing on an editor and his circle, is
questions.explanation: Anthills of the Savannah examines political corruption and dictatorship in a fictional West African state through the eyes of three friends.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Chinua Achebe's novel 'Arrow of God' centres on Ezeulu, the chief priest of the god
questions.explanation: Arrow of God follows Ezeulu, chief priest of the deity Ulu, as he struggles to maintain his authority amid colonial interference.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Amos Tutuola's novel 'The Palm-Wine Drinkard' is notable for its blend of Yoruba folklore with a narrator who journeys into the
options: sea to trade with European merchants
land of the dead in search of his dead palm-wine tapster
capital city to seek a government job
questions.explanation: The novel follows a palm-wine drinker's fantastical journey into the spirit world (Deads' Town) to bring back his dead tapster.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Ngugi wa Thiong'o's novel 'Weep Not, Child' is set against the backdrop of the
options: Mau Mau uprising against British colonial rule in Kenya
questions.explanation: Weep Not, Child depicts a Kenyan family's suffering and hopes during the Mau Mau struggle against British colonial rule.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Ngugi wa Thiong'o's novel 'A Grain of Wheat' focuses on the days surrounding Kenya's independence and the moral reckoning of characters over
options: the construction of a new railway
past betrayals during the struggle for freedom
an outbreak of famine in the countryside
questions.explanation: A Grain of Wheat examines guilt, heroism, and betrayal among villagers as Kenya approaches independence from British rule.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Cyprian Ekwensi's novel 'Jagua Nana' portrays the life of an ageing, glamorous woman navigating survival in the streets of
questions.explanation: Jagua Nana follows its titular character through the vibrant, often harsh, urban life of Lagos in the years around independence.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Elechi Amadi's novel 'The Concubine' is set in a traditional Igbo village and centres on Ihuoma, a beautiful woman whose suitors
options: unite to found a new village
all become wealthy through her influence
questions.explanation: The Concubine follows Ihuoma, whose suitors meet tragic, mysterious deaths, ultimately attributed to her being the wife of a jealous sea-god.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Buchi Emecheta's novel 'The Joys of Motherhood' critically examines the hardships faced by a Nigerian woman named
options: Kambili, a teenager in a strict household
Nnu Ego, as wife and mother in a patriarchal society
questions.explanation: The Joys of Motherhood follows Nnu Ego's difficult life as she struggles to fulfil the demanding, often unrewarded, roles of wife and mother.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie's novel 'Half of a Yellow Sun' is set primarily against the backdrop of the
questions.explanation: Half of a Yellow Sun follows several characters through the turbulence and devastation of the Nigerian Civil War of the late 1960s.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie's novel 'Purple Hibiscus' centres on a teenage girl, Kambili, growing up under the strict rule of her
questions.explanation: Purple Hibiscus portrays Kambili's coming of age within a household dominated by her father Eugene's rigid, abusive religious authority.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Charles Dickens' novel 'Great Expectations' follows the moral and social development of an orphan boy named
questions.explanation: Great Expectations traces Pip's journey from a humble blacksmith's apprentice to a young gentleman shaped by secret benefaction and hard lessons.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Charles Dickens' novel 'Oliver Twist' follows an orphan boy who falls in with a gang of pickpockets in
questions.explanation: Oliver Twist depicts the hardships of an orphan navigating the workhouses and criminal underworld of nineteenth-century London.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Jane Austen's novel 'Pride and Prejudice' centres on the evolving relationship between Elizabeth Bennet and
questions.explanation: Pride and Prejudice traces the shifting relationship between the spirited Elizabeth Bennet and the proud, initially aloof Mr Darcy.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Emily Bronte's novel 'Wuthering Heights' is centred on the intense, destructive love between Catherine Earnshaw and
questions.explanation: Wuthering Heights is driven by the passionate, ultimately tragic bond between Catherine and the brooding orphan Heathcliff.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: George Orwell's novel 'Animal Farm' is an allegory of the Russian Revolution in which farm animals overthrow their
questions.explanation: Animal Farm allegorises the Russian Revolution and its aftermath through the animals' rebellion against their exploitative farmer, Mr Jones.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: In George Orwell's 'Animal Farm', the pigs who eventually come to dominate the farm are led principally by
options: Old Major, throughout the entire novel
questions.explanation: Napoleon, a ruthless pig, gradually seizes total control of the farm, coming to mirror the tyranny the animals originally rebelled against.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: George Orwell's novel '1984' depicts a totalitarian society ruled by an omnipresent figure known as
questions.explanation: 1984 portrays a dystopian surveillance state dominated by the Party and its symbolic, all-seeing leader, Big Brother.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Mary Shelley's novel 'Frankenstein' tells the story of a scientist who creates a living being and is subsequently
options: protected from all consequence by the creature's loyalty
haunted by the tragic consequences of his creation
elected to lead his country's scientific council
rewarded by his university for the discovery
questions.explanation: Frankenstein follows Victor Frankenstein's growing horror and guilt as his creature brings tragedy upon him and his loved ones.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Daniel Defoe's novel 'Robinson Crusoe' recounts the survival of a shipwrecked man alone on an island, where he later encounters a man he names
questions.explanation: Robinson Crusoe rescues a native man from cannibals and names him Friday, after the day of their meeting, and the two form a bond.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Harper Lee's novel 'To Kill a Mockingbird' is narrated by a young girl named Scout, whose father, Atticus Finch, defends a black man named
options: Tom Robinson, wrongly accused of rape
questions.explanation: To Kill a Mockingbird centres on Atticus Finch's defence of Tom Robinson, a black man falsely accused of raping a white woman in the segregated American South.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: The Nigerian poet and playwright who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986 is
questions.explanation: Wole Soyinka became the first African Nobel laureate in Literature, honoured in 1986 for his body of work spanning drama, poetry, and prose.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Christopher Okigbo, a celebrated Nigerian poet known for the collection 'Labyrinths', died while fighting in the
questions.explanation: Okigbo, one of Africa's most influential modern poets, was killed in 1967 fighting on the Biafran side of the Nigerian Civil War.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: The Senegalese poet and statesman celebrated for developing the concept of 'Negritude' alongside writers such as Aime Cesaire is
questions.explanation: Leopold Sedar Senghor, Senegal's first president, was also a leading poet and a founding figure of the Negritude literary and cultural movement.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: The Negritude movement, which shaped much early African and Caribbean poetry, primarily sought to
options: promote unquestioning assimilation into European culture
affirm and celebrate black identity, culture, and heritage against colonial denigration
advocate for a return to pre-literate societies
reject all forms of African oral tradition
questions.explanation: Negritude emerged as a literary and ideological movement affirming pride in black identity and culture in response to colonial racism.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Kofi Awoonor, a major Ghanaian poet, is known for drawing heavily on the oral traditions of the
questions.explanation: Kofi Awoonor's poetry is deeply rooted in Ewe oral tradition and dirge forms, blending them with modern poetic techniques.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Niyi Osundare, a prominent contemporary Nigerian poet, is well known for his collection
questions.explanation: Niyi Osundare's The Eye of the Earth reflects his characteristic concern with nature, ecology, and social justice.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: A recurring concern in much African poetry addressing colonialism is the
options: clash between indigenous African values and imposed Western culture
rejection of any interest in nature or the land
questions.explanation: Much African poetry engages critically with the tensions between traditional African values and the disruptions brought by colonial rule.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Dennis Brutus, a South African poet, is best known for poetry that protested against
options: apartheid and racial oppression in South Africa
questions.explanation: Dennis Brutus's poetry, much of it written during his imprisonment, powerfully condemns the injustices of apartheid South Africa.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: The Nigerian poem 'Vanity' by Ezenwa-Ohaeto and similar Nigerian poetry often draw heavily on proverbs and imagery rooted in
options: African oral tradition and everyday communal life
questions.explanation: Much modern African poetry consciously incorporates proverbs, oral idioms, and imagery drawn from communal African life and tradition.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.text: Okot p'Bitek, the Ugandan poet famous for 'Song of Lawino', wrote the poem as a lament by a rural woman against her husband's
options: decision to marry a second wife
rejection of traditional Acholi customs in favour of Western ways
questions.explanation: Song of Lawino gives voice to Lawino's complaint against her husband Ocol's scorn for Acholi tradition in favour of Western values.
